recipes.name: Caramel Apple Pork Chops
ingredients_raw: 2 medium tart apples - peeled, cored and sliced

steps.text: Place a medium baking dish into the oven and preheat to 175 degrees F (80 degrees C).

Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Brush chops lightly with oil and place into the hot pan. Cook until no longer pink in the center, 5 to 6 minutes per side. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read 145 degrees F (63 degrees C). Transfer to the baking dish in the preheated oven to keep warm.
Stir brown sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg, salt, and pepper together in a small bowl.

Melt butter in a skillet over medium-low heat. Stir in apples and brown sugar mixture. Cover and cook until apples are just tender, about 5 minutes. Leaving the sauce in the skillet, remove apples with a slotted spoon and arrange over pork chops; keep warm in the oven.
Continue to cook sauce, uncovered, until thickened slightly, 2 to 3 minutes.
Remove pork chops from the oven. Spoon sauce over top and sprinkle with pecans.

raw_recipe.headline: Caramel Apple Pork Chops
raw_recipe.description: Juicy pork chops with apples team up with buttery pecans in this comforting dinner that’s spiced with warm cinnamon and nutmeg for fall flavor.

review.reviewBody: I first grabbed this recipe in 2003 and have been making it ever since. I have made a few alterations/shortcuts I thought others might like to know. 1) I throw the chops in a marinade overnight of 2x apple juice to soy. The sweet and salt help make the chops even juicer. 2) I always make at least double if not 4 times the sauce or there is arguing... :) so when time is short or I just don't feel like peeling all those apples, I buy 2 cans of the higher priced pie filling and put that in the frying pan used for browning with a stick of butter.(scrape up the good bits.) It usually has the right amount of spices built right in so I just heat through. Arrange over top the chops in a baking pan. Bake covered in foil at 350 for 20-25 minutes. Remove foil - sprinkle with brown sugar and chopped pecans - bake 15 mins more for carmelize and crunch. DELICIOUS! Pairs great with butternut squash or sweet potatoes and corn or green beans. Homemade honey wheat bread is sure to disappear. I pour all pan juices over the servings for mopping. Every year when the weather turns cold here, the family starts asking "Is it time for apple pork chops??" :)

After browning the pork chops I placed them in a steamer basket in pressure cooker/instant pot over water with cinnamon and nutmeg for 20 min. Was beyond fork tender and infused with flavor!!!! I added raisins and the pecans to the brown sugar mixture( doubled sauce amounts)also used green apples.

seriously this is delicious on the stovetop but apples and pork are meant to be together . But I Like to use bigger chops(3/4 -1 inch thick) so I seared them on both sides first and baked the pork and apples together in a covered dish. The pork will be so juicy the apples will get some subtle pork flavor.Then finished the apples on the stove with a little vanilla and extra brown sugar. It smells amazing too.

I just made this and it was wonderful. The pork chops were so juicy and the sauce very flavorful. Every bit of it is gone. Followed a lot of comments that i read- Marinated with soy sauce and apple cider 2:1 ratio and added a little oil and apple cider vinegar to marinade. This makes the chops soooo moist. I salted the chops then pan seared them, covered them with sauce, and baked them in 13x9 pan on 350 covered 25 min. and uncovered 15min.to caramelize sauce on top. I made 4 times the sauce that the receipe called for. I sauteed an onion into the butter at the beginning of making the sauce. Then added the spices, sugar, and apples to the mixture, cooked it for 15 min beofre covering the chops with it. Everyone is still licking their fingers. I served this with mashed potatos and acorn squash. The squah really complimented this dish.

Great recipe. 
I seasoned the pork with Black Pep and Salt and seared it for several mins on both sides than finished it in the oven 450F for about 20 mins. Came out crispy with the apples and used the remaining juices for the sauce.
Very delicious. Followed some suggestions by tripling the sauce ingredients and baking at 350 for 30 minutes, after browning. Next time I will add a T of cornstarch to the sauce as it was very thin.

I used a 4lbs whole pork tenderloin, topped with Apple butter cooked in a crockpot until temperature reached 145 degrees, removed to let rest, I made the sauce while doing so, added the Apple Butter sauce from the crockpot, omitted the nutmeg.

I decided to brine the pork chops before using this recipe. My brine was 1 c cider vinegar, 1/4 c salt, 2/3 c brown sugar, 2 t mustard powder and 2 c water. I let them sit in brine for about 2 hours, then rinsed super well, dried them and proceeded with this recipe. I followed the suggestion to carmalize some onion and add double the ingredients for the sauce. Meanwhile, I browned the pork chops in another pan, then poured the sauce on top of the chops. Covered, baked at 350 for 40 minutes, then removed cover and baked another 15. 
My family really enjoyed these chops - they came out very tender and tasty!

Wow! This is delicious! For sides, I made stuffing with onion, celery, mushrooms, chopped fresh sage and parsley from the herb garden, and corn cut from the cob and sautéed briefly in butter. Great fall flavors! After browning the chops and topping with the apples, I baked at 350, covered, about 20 minutes while the stuffing baked. Added a bit of cider to the sauce and reduced to syrupy consistency, then drizzled over chops and apples before serving. This recipe is a keeper!

Good recipe. I bumped up the spices by 50% which worked well (for me). Take care not to overdo the pork chops, and best to cover them while they are keeping warm in the oven. I did not get a lot of sauce out of it, but am fine with that as the apples lent it enough moisture. I will make this again.
It's the best when cooked in a crockpot, doubling the sauce, very tender! Wonderful recipe!
I think I overcooked the chops. They needed more flavor
Don't need to keep warm in oven.
Very tasty and great combination of flavors. Only change I made was to double the apples and the caramel just to have some extra. Will add this to dinner rotation. Thanks
Added some carmelized walnuts to mine This was quick and easy with mashed and peas
I like this recipe, but definitely need to make extra sauce- at least double. The only thing is that my partner and I find the leftovers to be very dry. Does anyone have any suggestions?
Didn’t change a thing, just doubled the sauce!
Quick, delicious and inexpensive dinner entree.
